title: Работа на тик по потокам: начало главы (4l) и конец (e5); R2 → P0 → R2 → R3
source: ntsd-2.4 at 5f5a8ee4: rt-4l-pending-loading-20261007.json, rt-e5-emit-consumes-20261010.json, rt-r2-presenter-thread-parked-20261009.json, rt-r2b-presenter-remeasured-20261010.json, rt-p0-main-on-fast-cores-20261010.json, rt-r2-presenter-thread-20261010.json, rt-r3-release-thread-20261010.json
caveat: One phone (Galaxy A12, Helio P35: CPUs 0-3 at 2.3 GHz, 4-7 at 1.8 GHz), debuggable build (local.ntsd.port), shipping flags from 4aa on (no dynamic exclusivity checks); scripted match (vs: computer vs computer, bodies 300->1800; Demo: eight computer fighters) with music, sounds and network off, no frame capture, the harness's virtual clock (8 ms per message-loop iteration). Compute per tick per thread from schedstat between bodies 600 and 1500 (tools/crossplatform/android_speed.py); not wall time. The sum over threads is CPU work per tick, not a frame time: the threads run at the same time on different cores. 4l had no Demo measurement (the Demo was first measured on 8 Oct).

cores.finding: while re-measuring R2 (rtr2b, rtr2c) the A12's threads were sampled during the Demo (/proc/<pid>/task/*/stat field 39 once a second): with the render thread busy the scheduler ran the main thread mostly on the slower cluster (CPUs 5–7, 1.8 GHz; CPUs 0–3 run at 2.3 GHz). An experiment with R2, the presenter on CPUs 4–7 and the main thread on 0–3 (exp-r2d, hard-coded) gave Demo main 13.10 -> 12.43 and render 10.40 -> 5.91, vs main 12.74 -> 11.94 and render 12.23 -> 7.94; this step is its main-thread half

r2b.result: render −4.0 ms in vs and −4.3 ms in the Demo (both under 8 ms); the main thread is unchanged in vs (+0.05) but still +0.57 ms in the Demo, where main is the frame's limit. Not committed: next, R2c pins the presenter to the other CPU cluster (CPUs 4–7, separate L2) to test whether the Demo's main-thread cost is cache contention
